messages:
tony_acme: Hey team — onboarding AcmeCorp with Azure Key Vault behind Private Endpoint. When our app calls your rewrap endpoint we get 403. Error from our side: `Forbidden: unwrapKey permission denied`.
sam (support): Thanks, Tony. Can you paste the exact API call and a short snippet of the error log? Also which deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)?
tony_acme: We're on Private (VPC install). Calling Redwood private-controlplane rewrap API via our VNet peering. Here's the HTTP error body:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"operation failed: unwrapKey not allowed for principal"}
```
neha (kms-eng): Quick checklist: 1) Key access policy vs RBAC in Azure? 2) Is the SPN using the private endpoint's outbound IP? 3) Key permissions include `unwrapKey`/`wrapKey` for current key version?
jordan (infra): Also check that the service principal is added to the vault's access policies OR has Key Vault CryptoUser role if using RBAC. Private Endpoint can still block token exchange if DNS isn't resolving to the Private Link address.
maria (security): And audit logs — we need to confirm whether Azure Key Vault audit shows a failed UnwrapKey call or if the request never hit Key Vault (which implies network/DNS issue).
tony_acme: We're using Azure AD app (client credentials) as our SP. We assigned Key Vault CryptoUser on the vault to that SPN. DNS for vault.mycompany.priv resolves to the private endpoint IP from our app host. The Key Vault diagnostic logs show nothing around the timestamp.
sam (support): If Key Vault diagnostics show nothing, likely the traffic isn't reaching Key Vault. Can you share curl against the control plane rewrap endpoint (redwood-private.example/rewrap) sanitized? Also paste the caller IP we see in your app logs.
tony_acme: Caller IP is 10.2.3.45 (within VNet). Here's the request we forward to Redwood control plane (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/keys/kv-key/rewrap
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
{
  "ciphertext": "...",
  "wrapping_algorithm": "rsa-oaep"
}
```
neha (kms-eng): Important nuance: For envelope rewrap we sometimes do a server-side unwrap using Redwood-managed intermediate key and then call customer KMS to rewrap. In Private mode, Redwood's control plane may not have direct network route to your Key Vault unless a managed egress path is configured. Are you using the default private deployment networking (no egress NAT)?
jordan (infra): Exactly. Private deployments often require an egress NAT or an outbound proxy configured so the control plane can reach customer KMS. If there's no outbound path, the rewrap will fail in our runtime but should still show up in Key Vault logs once attempted. Tony said no logs — suggests request never left control plane or got blocked before Key Vault.
infra-bot: Deploy job #3842 completed on prod-controlplane (revision a3f2). No errors reported.
maria (security): For RBAC specifically confirm these in the Key Vault resource: 1) SPN has role assignment at vault scope for Key Vault CryptoUser or built-in Key Vault Crypto Officer, 2) Access policies are not conflicting (if vault still has classic access policies turned on), 3) Key's key_ops includes wrapKey/unwrapKey. Also confirm key is not marked as 'disabled'.
neha (kms-eng): Can you run this Azure CLI from a host inside the VNet and paste output? `az keyvault key show --vault-name <vault> --name <key>` and `az role assignment list --assignee <spn>`
tony_acme: Ran those. Key shows `key_ops: ["encrypt","decrypt","wrapKey","unwrapKey"]`. Role assignment shows `Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User` at resource group scope for the SPN.
sam (support): That role name sounds like a custom/builtin mismatch. Can you confirm the principal type is ServicePrincipal not Group? Also check Azure AD conditional access or managed identity restrictions.
neha (kms-eng): Another angle: are you using key version pinning? If Redwood is trying to call a different key version (older) we can get 403 for that principal if the role was added at resource level after version created. But usually key permissions are per-key, not per-version.
jordan (infra): Tony, does your Key Vault have 'Purge protection' or 'Soft delete' enabled? Not likely related, but noting.
tony_acme: Principal is ServicePrincipal. No conditional access. Key vault has soft delete enabled. Also, we noticed when we try to call GenerateDataKey on AWS KMS equivalent it works — only Azure Key Vault rewrap fails.
maria (security): That hints at a control plane network problem. Try tcpdump from the control plane egress host (or request our support to collect pcap) to confirm whether requests leave Redwood control plane cluster.
sam (support): We'll spin up a diagnostic run. neha/jordan — can you check control plane egress routes for AcmeCorp tenant in Private cluster? We may need to set up NAT or a VNet peering for controlplane egress to vault.
neha (kms-eng): On our side: if outbound egress is blocked intentionally (security constraint), we support customer-provided rewrap by asking for encrypted key blobs and letting customer's runtime (in their VPC) do the final call. That's a manual workflow; documentation gap here. I'll add a note to internal docs.
jordan (infra): For immediate triage I recommend: 1) Tony: try hitting the Key Vault REST endpoint directly from an app host that uses the same VNet egress as Redwood (if you have a bastion) to confirm Azure logs appear. 2) We'll run connectivity checks from control plane to vault fqdn and ip.
tony_acme: Ok will try direct curl from bastion and report logs.
sam (support): Thanks. We'll also open a backend ticket to check NAT mappings for tenant 5467. Ticket #SUP-1628.
neha (kms-eng): Note for documentation: add a clear section about Private installations and KMS egress requirements, and sample `az role assignment`/`az keyvault` commands. I'll draft after triage.
tony_acme: Quick follow-up — is there a required Azure AD permission beyond Key Vault RBAC? Like `Managed Identity Operator` for our SP to allow Redwood to impersonate?
maria (security): No, Redwood doesn't impersonate customer SPNs. We authenticate to Key Vault using the credentials you provide. So ensure the credentials belong to a principal with wrap/unwrap rights. No extra MSFT permission needed on our side.
sam (support): Closing loop: Tony, please paste your bastion curl output when ready and we'll reconvene. :thumbsup:
